- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.33) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast decline to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.11 for 3+ days), model tends to overestimate future prices — apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early 30d horizon — if recent 7-day average is > 10% above 30d avg, reduce forecast by 3–8%.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.06–0.11), model often fails to capture short-term volatility — add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast range.
- If true outcome shows early drop after forecast peak, model often lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match true drop pattern.
- For 30d horizon, model tends to overestimate late-period decline — reduce forecast by 2–5% for last 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or negative.
